vt.analysis:
Type: OpenClaw Skill
Name: video-resizer-zh
Version: 1.0.8

The skill is a legitimate integration for the Sparki video processing service (sparki.io). It consists of bash scripts (edit_video.sh, upload_asset.sh, etc.) that use curl and jq to upload videos and poll for processing results. The instructions in SKILL.md are clearly aligned with the stated purpose of video resizing, and there is no evidence of data exfiltration, unauthorized execution, or malicious prompt injection.

llm.summary: The skill's code, instructions, and requested credentials are consistent with a video upload/resize workflow that calls Sparki's Business API; nothing requests unrelated secrets or surprising system access.

dimensions.detail: Name/description state a video resize workflow and the shipped scripts (upload_asset.sh, create_project.sh, get_project_status.sh, edit_video.sh) implement exactly that: upload an mp4, create a processing job, poll for completion, and return a pre-signed result URL. The required SPARKI_API_KEY and optional SPARKI_API_BASE align with calling the Sparki API.
dimensions.label: Purpose & Capability
dimensions.name: purpose_capability

dimensions.detail: SKILL.md and the scripts only direct the agent to read a user-supplied local mp4 file (checked for size/extension), call Sparki endpoints, and poll for results. There are no instructions to read other local files, shell histories, or unrelated credentials, nor to transmit data to unexpected endpoints beyond the configured Sparki API base.
dimensions.label: Instruction Scope
dimensions.name: instruction_scope

dimensions.detail: No install spec; this is instruction + included shell scripts. No remote downloads or archive extraction. The only runtime requirements are standard CLI tools (curl, jq), which are reasonable for the described network/API interactions.
dimensions.label: Install Mechanism
dimensions.name: install_mechanism

dimensions.detail: The declared required env is just SPARKI_API_KEY (primaryEnv), which is appropriate. SKILL.md also documents optional SPARKI_API_BASE and the scripts read optional WORKFLOW_TIMEOUT and ASSET_TIMEOUT; those optional env vars are reasonable but are not listed in the declared requires.env metadata (minor documentation mismatch). No unrelated secrets or multiple external credentials are requested.
dimensions.label: Credentials
dimensions.name: environment_proportionality

dimensions.detail: always:false and the skill does not attempt to modify other skills or system-wide configs. It does not request permanent elevated privileges. Agent autonomous invocation is allowed by default (not a problem here) and appropriate for this kind of skill.
dimensions.label: Persistence & Privilege
dimensions.name: persistence_privilege

llm.guidance: This skill will upload the specific local .mp4 file you give it to Sparki (business-agent-api.sparki.io by default) using the SPARKI_API_KEY you configure. Before installing/using: 1) make sure you trust Sparki and are comfortable uploading the video content (privacy considerations and third‑party processing), 2) create an API key with minimal scope and rotate/revoke it when no longer needed, 3) confirm curl and jq are present and you run the script only on files you intend to upload, and 4) note that result URLs are pre-signed (README and scripts indicate 24‑hour links). The only small inconsistency is that the scripts accept optional env vars (WORKFLOW_TIMEOUT, ASSET_TIMEOUT) that are not listed in the metadata; this is informational rather than a functional or security mismatch.
